summary: Nobody walks you in: Custom says {senior member} walks you to the oath, and he stays in his seat, reading.
realLife: When he came to take his Senate seat in 1875, Mississippi's senior senator, James Alcorn, refused to escort him and kept reading a newspaper. Roscoe Conkling of New York crossed the chamber and walked with him.
gates: A custom of escort on record.
A grudge between you and {senior member} on record.
choices: take {stranger}'s arm when he crosses the floor

branches.when: the grudge goes back to a race
branches.then: You backed someone else against him once, and the record says why.
A tie, and a debt later votes read.
